operations_plan.summary: Add integral coaxial cylindrical retaining heads to both exposed axial ends of the two fixed endpoint through-shafts. The head diameter and thickness are not specified; use one common parametric head size that is larger than the mating link pivot bores, no larger than the surrounding link-end bosses, and positioned outside the outer link faces with running axial clearance.

steps.description: Identify the fixed long pins as the lower positive-X fixed pivot shaft and upper positive-X fixed pivot shaft in SEC_ENDPOINT_SHAFTS. Use cylindrical shank faces 30 and 121 to recover their existing Z-axis centerlines. Confirm that the lower shaft passes through the lower fixed platform bore face 79 and link bores 27 and 186, and that the upper shaft passes through the upper fixed platform bore face 118 and link bores 156 and 214. Preserve these axes, shank diameters, bearing lengths, and all existing joint locations.

Define a shared retaining-head diameter and axial thickness for the fixed shafts. Because no numerical dimensions are supplied, flag the dimensions as unresolved and derive them parametrically: the diameter must exceed the maximum mating pivot-bore diameter represented by faces 27, 186, 156, and 214, while remaining within the radial envelope of the associated endpoint bosses represented by faces 11, 170, 158, and 216. Select the minimum practical axial thickness for a rigid retaining shoulder, preferably matching any established visible pin-end proportion. Reserve a small positive axial running clearance between each head's inward shoulder and the adjacent outboard link face so the links remain free to rotate and are not clamped.

On the rear terminal planar faces 31 and 122, create one circular sketch per shaft, concentric with the axis recovered from shank faces 30 and 121. Set both circles to the shared retaining-head diameter from OP_001_STEP_002. Pad each circle axially toward the rear, away from the linkage assembly, by the selected head thickness and fuse it to its parent shaft solid. The resulting inward annular shoulder must remain outboard of the rear link faces with the specified running clearance.

Repeat the concentric circular-pad construction on front terminal planar faces 33 and 124. Extrude toward the front, away from the linkage assembly, using the same diameter and thickness as the rear heads, then fuse the pads into shaft solids 1 and 6. Keep the inward head shoulders outside the front link stack and preserve positive axial clearance from the adjacent link faces.

Finish the four new fixed-shaft heads as cylindrical retaining disks. If an edge break is required for manufacturability, apply only a small equal chamfer or fillet to each exposed outer circular edge; do not round away the inward retaining shoulders or alter the cylindrical shanks and bearing surfaces. Verify that each head overlaps the mating link-hole radius and does not exceed the endpoint-boss radial envelope.

operations_plan.summary: Add matching integral cylindrical retaining heads to both exposed ends of the lower and upper sliding endpoint through-shafts, then verify that all eight new heads retain the link arms without affecting rotation, slot translation, or platform travel.

steps.description: Identify the sliding long pins as the lower negative-X sliding pivot shaft and upper negative-X sliding pivot shaft. Recover their coaxial Z directions from cylindrical shank faces 38 and 126. Confirm that the lower slider engages lower slot faces 68 through 78 and 80 and link bores 157 and 215, while the upper slider engages upper slot faces 107 through 117 and 119 and link bores 26 and 185. Preserve the existing shank diameters, axes, endpoint positions, and freedom to translate along X inside the slots.

Apply the same retaining-head diameter, thickness, and axial-clearance convention established in OP_001_STEP_002. Check the diameter against sliding-link bore faces 157, 215, 26, and 185 and against endpoint-boss outer cylindrical faces 141, 199, 28, and 187. The dimensions remain unresolved numerically because the request supplies no diameter, thickness, or clearance; use the common fixed-shaft head parameters unless local boss geometry requires a smaller noninterfering diameter that still exceeds the pivot-hole diameter.

On rear terminal planar faces 39 and 127, sketch circles concentric with shank faces 38 and 126. Pad the circles axially toward the rear by the common head thickness and fuse them into sliding-shaft solids 3 and 7. Locate the inward annular shoulders beyond the rear outboard link faces, maintaining running axial clearance throughout the allowed slot travel.

On front terminal planar faces 41 and 129, create matching concentric circular sketches and pad them axially toward the front, away from the assembly. Fuse the pads into solids 3 and 7. Maintain the same axial clearance from the front links as used on the fixed shafts so the new heads act only as axial stops and do not preload or clamp the sliding joints.

Apply the same optional small outer-edge chamfer or fillet used on the fixed-shaft heads while preserving square inward retaining shoulders. Confirm that the head disks remain outside the link arms and do not enter either platform guide slot or contact the red platform side faces during translation.

Perform an assembly interference and kinematic check over the full intended scissor range. Verify that all four endpoint shafts now have cylindrical heads at both exposed ends; every head diameter is larger than its associated link pivot hole; the links cannot pass axially over the heads; and positive clearance remains between each inward head shoulder and the neighboring link. Confirm unrestricted rotation at all endpoint bores, unrestricted X translation of shafts 3 and 7 through the lower and upper guide slots, unchanged center-pivot behavior, unchanged platform spacing and parallelism, and no collision with the platforms or adjacent components. Do not modify the platform solids, link solids, central pins, slots, or existing shaft axes during this validation.
